summary.text: The source declares a periodic refresh with a 60-second default, selects places with missing or expired forecasts, and attempts a refresh for each place. A per-place exception is logged as FORECAST_RETRY, allowing the loop to move on. The saved view covers cached returns, fixture/live-provider paths, response and transformation outcomes, and persistence/outbox effects. The linked forecasts-publish-pending view describes separate follow-on work; this captured process does not prove it ran afterward. The external-provider interaction is declared but not established by this evidence. Scheduler activation, provider responses, database commits, and event delivery remain unverified.

blocks.text: Live mode requires a nonblank MET_USER_AGENT. It stores nextAttempt in a private in-memory map keyed by place ID, checks it before the request and sets a 60-second deadline before sending. The GET uses coordinates truncated down to four decimal places, a 20-second timeout, User-Agent, gzip and an optional If-Modified-Since. Each response sets expiry from Expires or a one-hour fallback. For 429, numeric Retry-After sets the next attempt with a 60-second minimum; other statuses set it to expiry, before status handling. The lifetime of the runtime instance is not established.

blocks.text: Missing live configuration, an active wait or an unaccepted provider status prevents normal refresh. Statuses 200 and 203 can proceed; a 304 needs an existing cache entry for the reuse branch.

blocks.text: Fixture input and accepted provider bodies use the same transformation. Up to six periods are prepared; temperature must be numeric and the result must not be empty.

blocks.text: Parsing or validation errors prevent the normal write path. Missing or nonnumeric rain becomes null and a missing symbol becomes unknown; missing numeric temperature or an empty forecast is rejected.
